tool_input.message:
Delta review of f9bbf00..HEAD complete: 6 findings — 3 Critical (all in af9b941's drift guard, two empirically falsified), 3 Important (stale prose in store.go, K3's purge claim, K8's queue-position count). K1's classification logic and K3's mechanics are clean.

## Scope
9 commits, Go + docs. Skipped the JSONL audit state per your instruction. All five priority areas examined. Probes run against a scratch copy and reverted; `git status` is clean.

---

## CRITICAL (90-100)

### 1. The drift guard does not detect a fourth write site in a new file — confidence 96
`internal/mission/aborted_writer_drift_test.go:41-45`

The guard parses three hardcoded file paths. It does not walk the packages. I added this file and the test still passed:

```go
// internal/mission/zzprobe_driftcheck.go
package mission
func probeCancelRunningWorker(repoRoot, missionID, delegationID, closedAt string) error {
	return CloseDelegationSkeleton(repoRoot, missionID, delegationID, DelegationVerdictAborted, closedAt)
}
```
`go test -run TestAbortedVerdictWriteSites` → PASS.

This is exactly the scenario the test's own doc comment names ("a 'cancel a running worker' command is the obvious future candidate"). Worse, `CloseDelegationSkeleton` and `CloseDelegation` are exported, and `cmd/ethos/mission.go` and `internal/mcp/mission_tools.go` both already import `mission` — neither is scanned. An `ethos mission cancel` command is invisible to this guard in every plausible location except the three files that already have a write site.

Fix: walk `internal/mission`, `internal/hook`, `internal/mcp`, and `cmd/ethos` with `parser.ParseDir` (skipping `_test.go`) instead of listing three paths.

### 2. The guard's "write position" definition misses composite-literal and return shapes — confidence 92
`internal/mission/aborted_writer_drift_test.go:116-127`

`Visit` only matches when the identifier's immediate parent is `*ast.AssignStmt` or `*ast.CallExpr`. Appending these two functions **to store.go itself** (a listed file) still passed:

```go
func probeStructLiteralWriter() Delegation { return Delegation{Verdict: DelegationVerdictAborted} }
func probeReturnWriter() string            { return DelegationVerdictAborted }
```
`go test -run TestAbortedVerdictWriteSites` → PASS.

`KeyValueExpr` (a struct-literal field — the most natural way to stamp a verdict onto a record) and `ReturnStmt` (a helper that hands the constant to a caller that writes it) are both uncovered. A package-level `var abortVerdict = DelegationVerdictAborted` is also invisible, since `enclosingFuncsWritingAbortedVerdict` only walks `FuncDecl` bodies.

Positive control confirmed the guard works for the call-arg shape: adding a `CloseDelegationSkeleton(..., DelegationVerdictAborted, ...)` call to store.go produced a clear, actionable failure naming all four sites and what to re-justify. The message quality is good — the detection surface is the problem.

Fix: add `*ast.KeyValueExpr`, `*ast.ReturnStmt`, and `*ast.ValueSpec` to the matched parent set, or invert the rule (match everything *except* `BinaryExpr`, `CaseClause`, and the const declaration).

### 3. The guard's stated safety rationale is false, and the CHANGELOG repeats it — confidence 93
`internal/mission/aborted_writer_drift_test.go:14-16`, `CHANGELOG.md:107-110`

The test says the three sites are "all of which fire BEFORE a worker process starts." Its own `wantSites` includes `store.go:Close`. That third writer is `internal/mission/store.go:1078` — `Store.Close`'s sweep maps `VerdictEscalate` to `DelegationVerdictAborted`, and `closeDelegationSkeletons` (store.go:1225) applies it to every delegation still at `verdict: open`, i.e. spawns that were admitted and whose workers ran. It does not fire before a worker starts.

`countBlockingDelegations`'s own comment (store.go:1845-1856) gets this right and gives the actual argument: the Close sweep is unreachable from `countBlockingDelegations` because Abandon refuses unless the mission is `StatusOpen`. That is the real invariant.

`CHANGELOG.md:107-110` states it more strongly and equally wrongly: "`verdict: aborted` — written only by the `max_delegation_depth` refusal or the content-hash-gate refusal." There is a third writer, and the test the same commit series added enumerates it.

Why it matters beyond pedantry: the guard exists to make the next maintainer re-justify a fourth writer. It hands them the wrong criterion. "Fires before the worker starts" would wave through a writer that stamps `aborted` on an *open* mission's delegation — the one thing that would actually break the exclusion. The correct criterion is "no writer may stamp `aborted` on a delegation belonging to a mission that is still open."

---

## IMPORTANT (80-89)

### 4. `Store.Abandon`'s own doc comments still describe the pre-DES-076 gate — confidence 88
`internal/mission/store.go:1234-1256` and `1335-1344`

K2/K5 fixed this exact sentence in four places — `cmd/ethos/mission.go`'s `--help`, `internal/mcp/mission_tools.go`'s tool description, `internal/enable/guide/CLAUDE.md`, and `docs/mission-abandon.md`. The function itself was missed:

- store.go:1252-1256: "Any sign that work started — a delegation record (even a still-open skeleton), or a result for any round — refuses the transition… There is no override flag here either." Both halves are now false: `verdict: aborted` never blocks, and `--disclaim` is an override for gate 1.
- store.go:1335-1342 (the Gate 1 inline comment): "Any entry under delegations/ — open, closed, any verdict — … blocks Abandon UNLESS an operator has explicitly disclaimed it." Omits the automatic aborted exclusion, which is the very thing this branch added.

This is the authoritative comment — the one a maintainer reads before touching the gate — and it now contradicts the four surfaces you just corrected. Same class as K5; the class fix stopped one file short.

### 5. K3's "purge closes the abnormal-death gap" claim does not hold on the CLI-reachable path — confidence 87
`internal/session/store.go:222-227`, `CHANGELOG.md:189-198`

`deleteFiles`'s doc comment and the CHANGELOG both say `Purge`/`PurgeTombstoned` are "exactly the crash-recovery paths that needed this," closing the gap for sessions killed by SIGKILL or a closed terminal.

But `ethos session purge` calls `PurgeTombstoned` (`cmd/ethos/session.go:881`), and `PurgeTombstoned` refuses — without ever reaching `deleteFiles` — precisely on crash artifacts:
- `store.go:355-359`: unreadable roster → refuse unless `--force`. The function's own comment calls this "a crash artifact — precisely the state most likely to hold unsealed lines."
- `store.go:491-502`: `unsealed > 0 || probeFailed` → refuse unless `--force`. A SIGKILL'd session is the canonical holder of unsealed audit lines.

So the headline scenario (abnormal death) is the one most likely to hit the refusal and leave the sidecars in place. The gap closes only for cleanly-sealed stale sessions, or under `--force`.

Compounding it: `TestStore_Purge_ClearsMissionSidecars` (store_test.go) exercises `Purge()`, which no CLI command calls — the only non-test caller is `PurgeTombstoned`. The CLI-reachable path has no sidecar-clearing test at all, and none of its refusal branches are covered.

Fix: either soften the claim to name the guard, or clear the sidecars on the refusal path too (they are not audit state; the tombstone guard exists to protect unsealed audit lines, not mission bindings), plus a `PurgeTombstoned` test.

### 6. K8's "N pending dispatch(es) are ahead of it and will be matched first" over-counts — confidence 85
`cmd/ethos/mission.go:2217-2220`, `internal/mcp/mission_tools.go:299-302`

`dispatchBoundMessage` counts every same-worker entry ahead of `missionID` regardless of its mission's status. `matchDispatchPending` does not: `pretooluse_dispatch.go:301-311` skips **and clears** an entry whose mission is provably non-open, and `:312-319` skips an unresolvable one. Neither will be "matched first."

Reachable without exotic faults: `ClearMissionBindings` only clears the *calling* session's sidecar, so closing m-A from a different terminal (or any session with no ethos session context) leaves m-A's pending entry in session S. The next `dispatch --worker bwk` in S then reports "1 pending dispatch(es) for bwk are ahead of it and will be matched first (m-A)" — when in fact the next `bwk` spawn clears m-A as stale and binds m-B.

K8 exists to stop this message from lying about queue position. It now lies in the other direction. Fix: filter `sameWorker` through the same open/stale/unresolvable classification, or hedge the wording ("…are ahead of it in the queue; the oldest still-open one will be matched first").

Related, minor (below the reporting bar, noting for completeness): both implementations discard `ReadDispatchPending`'s `warnings` slice (`entries, _, err :=` / `entries, _, rErr :=`). `matchDispatchPending:291-293` prints them. A symlinked or unreadable pending entry therefore silently drops out of the queue-position count with no operator signal.

---

## Examined and clean

**1. `052d18b` — `matchDispatchPending` three-way classification.** Clean. `classifyPendingEntry` (pretooluse_dispatch.go:376-389) is exhaustive over the store-error / Load-error / non-open / open cases; the switch has no fall-through hole. No viable entry can be misclassified — `pendingEntryOpen` requires a successful `Load` *and* `nonOpenReason == ""`. FIFO is preserved: `ReadDispatchPending` sorts oldest-first with a deterministic `MissionID` tiebreak (active.go:642), candidates are appended in iteration order, and `candidates[0]` is returned — the skip loop cannot reach past an earlier viable entry. A lone unresolvable entry falls through correctly (`len(candidates) == 0` → `""` → Tier A/B), pinned by `..._UnresolvableEntrySkipsNotBlocks`. Nothing is cleared but provably-non-open entries. `TestMatchDispatchPending_UnresolvableEntryDoesNotBlockNewerEntry` covers the head-of-line case directly and asserts the skipped entry survives. The one accepted cost — a permanently-unloadable entry re-emits its 4-line warning on every same-worker spawn forever — is named in the message with the `mission release` remedy.

**2. `6c601df` — `deleteFiles` clearing sidecars. Mechanics clean; only the claim (finding 5) is wrong.** All three `Clear*` primitives are no-op-on-missing (`active.go:414`, `:679`, `:779`), so no stderr spam on the overwhelmingly common no-sidecar case. `clearMissionSidecars` is strictly per-session-ID — no path by which purging session A touches session B's sidecars. `s.root` is the global root at the only non-test `session.NewStore` call site (`cmd/ethos/identity.go:161`), so the paths line up with what `mission.ClearActiveMission` expects. Ordering in `purgeOneTombstoned` is safe: `SessionBoundMissions` (store.go:456) reads before `deleteFiles` (store.go:524) deletes. Advisory log-and-continue is right here — a sidecar-clear failure must not strand a roster deletion mid-way, and it matches `session_end.go` and `runMissionRelease`. All `Delete` callers (`session_end.go:44`, `cmd/ethos/session.go:643`, `:699`) are genuine teardown paths, never live sessions.

**3. `af9b941` — drift guard.** Findings 1-3. The failure *message* is good: it lists actual vs. expected sites and states what to re-justify. Detection surface and rationale are the problems.

**4. `18bb940` — `bindDispatchedMission` read-back.** Ordering is right (read strictly after `WriteDispatchPending`, so the fresh entry is present and sorts last by mtime). It cannot fail the dispatch: a `ReadDispatchPending` error falls back to the original wording, and the not-found case has its own fallback with a comment explaining why it does not assert a position it cannot verify. Both CLI and MCP implementations are consistent, and both have tests. Only the over-count (finding 6) is wrong.

**5. Doc changes.** `docs/mission-abandon.md` (0c824ae) checked line-by-line against `countBlockingDelegations` and `DisclaimDelegation` — the two carve-outs, the three disclaim gates (`BoundVia`, `Verdict != open`, no double-disclaim), the "disclaim never touches the result gate" claim, and the decision table all match the code. Its internal Gate 2/Gate 3 numbering is self-consistent, though it is offset by one from the code comments' Gate 1/Gate 2 (not worth changing). `6c07b73`'s `--help` and MCP-description rewrites are accurate. `964cb93`'s DES-076 correction is accurate — I confirmed `readActiveMissionForDispatch` accepts only `BindOriginClaim` (`pretooluse_dispatch.go:209`), so a well-formed legacy `BindOriginDispatch` pair is genuinely refused, and the new test pins it. `60cec2f`'s K9 symmetry claim is correct: the out-of-order spawn consumes m-A, leaving only m-B for the second spawn, so it is a full swap, not a single misattribution. K11(b)'s new `TestHandlePreToolUse_DepthRefusalThenAbandonNeedsNoDisclaim` is a genuine end-to-end proof — it drives `enforceDelegationDepth` through the real hook and reads the verdict back off disk rather than injecting it. The only false doc claims are findings 3 and 5.

Suggested order: 1 and 2 together (one rewrite of the guard's detection), then 3 (drop the false rationale from the test and the CHANGELOG, replace with the reachability argument store.go:1845 already states), then 4, 6, 5.
